output:
**Two sugars and a spare Thursday**

Bridget has asked me to write this month’s piece for the volunteers’ blog, so I’d better start with the obvious: I’m not a saint. I’m a retired bookkeeper, 74, and on Thursday afternoons I push a tea trolley round the day therapy unit at Wensum Vale. That’s the job, more or less. People hear “hospice” and assume it must be either harrowing or terribly skilled. Mostly it’s tea, biscuits and remembering who takes what.

The practical bit first. The Thursday tea trolley runs from 1.30 to 4pm. We’re meant to be six volunteers on the rota. We’re four. Two left over the summer—one moved to Sheffield to be near her grandchildren, one had a knee op—and we’ve been two short ever since. The commitment is one Thursday a fortnight. Bridget does the induction, which takes about two hours, and there’s a short online food hygiene course which the hospice pays for. No nursing skills required. You need to be able to push a trolley, remember who takes what, and listen.

That last one matters more than it sounds. Mr Hollis, a retired signalman, takes two sugars and tells me about the 1953 floods every week, slightly differently each time. I’ve stopped correcting the dates. The bourbon biscuits always go first. We now hide a packet for the late group. I’m not saying this is the noble side of volunteering, but it keeps the peace.

On a Thursday the day unit sees about 14 to 18 patients. Many come for the art group, the hand massage, or just company. Most go home afterwards. It’s a sociable afternoon rather than a medical one. It’s not a sad place on a Thursday, mostly. It’s noisy and rather jolly. Sad days do happen, and the staff look after us when they do. I won’t pretend otherwise, but I won’t dwell on it either. Some weeks are hard. Most weeks I come home having laughed at something daft.

My first week I spilled an entire jug of milk over the trolley. A patient called Pat laughed so much she had to be given a tissue. She said it was the best afternoon she’d had in a month. I’ve tried to be less entertaining since, with mixed results.

I started in March 2022, about eighteen months after I retired from 41 years of bookkeeping, mostly for a builders’ merchant in Dereham. I had no regular reason to go out most weeks and drifted a bit in that time. Thursdays fixed that. I do it because I like it, not because I’m better than anyone. It gets me out, and the tea is decent. It turns out 41 years of keeping ledgers straight is quite handy for remembering who takes what. I didn’t expect that to be my transferable skill, but there we are.

We’re having a volunteer open afternoon on Tuesday 24 November at 2pm in the Willow Room. Tea and biscuits, no obligation. Come and see what it’s like. Or ring Bridget on the volunteering line. If two people read this and come along, we’ll be back to six, and I can stop hiding the bourbon biscuits quite so obviously.
